intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene.

checks.claim: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is caused by homozygous mutation in the MPV17 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We suggest that a novel homozygous p.R41Q mutation in MPV17 causes axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without hepatoencephalopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous MPV17 mutation to axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, which it compares to axonal CMT. It never uses the label CMT2EE, which is OMIM's own disease name.

paragraphs.text: Axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2EE (CMT2EE) is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with juvenile or adult onset. Affected individuals have distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs, along with distal sensory loss. They do not have the liver or brain involvement seen in Navajo neurohepatopathy, which is also caused by MPV17 mutations (Choi et al., 2015; Baumann et al., 2019).

checks.claim: CMT2EE is an autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: This study enrolled two autosomal recessive Korean families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (FC26 and FC355, Fig. 1a).
checks.explanation: The paper describes autosomal recessive families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.

checks.claim: CMT2EE has juvenile or adult onset.
checks.evidence_quote: MPV17 mutations in juvenile- and adult-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.explanation: The title states juvenile and adult onset.

checks.claim: Individuals with CMT2EE have distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: Neurologic examination at the age of 34 years revealed muscle weakness and atrophies of bilateral, distal muscles, predominantly in the lower limbs.

checks.claim: Individuals with CMT2EE have distal sensory loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Vibration and position senses were more severely disturbed than pain and touch senses.
checks.explanation: Sensory disturbance is described, and sensory responses were absent on nerve conduction testing. The paper does not explicitly call the sensory loss 'distal'.

checks.claim: Individuals with CMT2EE do not have the liver or brain involvement seen in Navajo neurohepatopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Both showed axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without liver and brain involvement

checks.claim: Navajo neurohepatopathy is also caused by MPV17 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in MPV17 cause the autosomal recessive disorder mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 6 (MTDPS6), also called Navajo neurohepatopathy (NNH).

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) reported 2 unrelated Korean patients, each born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents, with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Patient 1, a 34-year-old woman, first noticed weakness of the distal lower limbs at 9 years of age and began walking with short leg braces at 12 years. On examination at 34 years, she had bilateral distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs. She had severe atrophy of the intrinsic hand, foot, and calf muscles, flexion deformities of the interphalangeal joints, ankle joint deformity, and scoliosis. Vibration and position senses were more severely affected than pain and touch, and knee and ankle jerks were absent. Patient 2, a 22-year-old man, first had gait and balance problems at age 13 and began walking with short leg braces at 20 years. He had bilateral distal weakness and atrophy, flat feet, absent deep tendon reflexes in all extremities, and the same predominant loss of vibration and position sense. Neither patient had other features of Navajo neurohepatopathy, such as hepatomegaly, cognitive impairment, ophthalmoplegia, or corneal scarring. Serum lactate was mildly elevated in both patients (2.1 and 1.9 mmol/L).

paragraphs.text: Electrophysiologic studies in the patients of Choi et al. (2015) showed loss of sural sensory nerve action potentials early in the disease. Median and ulnar nerves had reduced motor conduction velocities and CMAPs, peroneal and tibial CMAPs could not be elicited, and no sensory responses were recordable. Visual and brainstem auditory evoked potentials were normal. Muscle MRI of the lower leg showed severe atrophy and fatty replacement mainly in the soleus muscles, with relative sparing of the tibialis posterior and lateral gastrocnemius; the authors considered this pattern consistent with length-dependent axonal degeneration. Brain MRI was normal in both patients. In patient 1, sural nerve biopsy at 34 years showed complete loss of large and medium-sized myelinated fibers, with no demyelination, remyelination, or onion bulbs. In patient 2, vastus lateralis muscle biopsy at 22 years showed a few ragged-red fibers and subsarcolemmal accumulation of enlarged mitochondria.

paragraphs.text: Blakely et al. (2012) reported a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, with a phenotype the authors considered similar to the classic form of Navajo neurohepatopathy. He had walking difficulties from age 14 years that progressed to bilateral foot drop, together with distal sensory loss, distal muscle wasting, and absent tendon reflexes. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Unlike the patients described by Choi et al. (2015) and Baumann et al. (2019), he also had leukoencephalopathy on brain MRI, raised CSF protein and lactate, mild hepatomegaly, and patchy hepatic steatosis with early bridging fibrosis on liver biopsy. His muscle biopsy showed ragged-red fibers, about 20% COX-deficient fibers, and multiple mtDNA deletions with normal mtDNA copy number. His sister died of a progressive hepatitis that began at age 9 years.

paragraphs.text: Choi et al. (2015) performed whole-exome sequencing on 3 members of each of 2 unrelated Korean families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. In the affected individual of each family they found the same homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene, resulting in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation, and in both families a mutant allele was putatively inherited from each parent. The mutation was absent from 300 controls and 302 in-house exomes and was not in dbSNP142 or the 1000 Genomes Project database. It was present at very low frequency in the Exome Sequencing Project (0.00008) and ExAC (0.00002471) databases. In NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells, knockdown of Mpv17 reduced cell proliferation and viability under oxidative stress, and expression of the R41Q mutant protein significantly inhibited cell proliferation. The authors suggested that both loss of normal MPV17 function and harmful effects of the mutant protein might affect neuronal function.

agent.process_note: I read all three files in full: Blakely 2012 and Choi 2015 as full text, Baumann 2019 as abstract only. The causal gene (MPV17) and homozygous recessive inheritance come from Choi 2015 and Baumann 2019. For Baumann 2019 only the abstract was available, so ages at onset, ancestry, consanguinity, family sizes, clinical details and the exact protein-level effect of c.376-9T>G could not be checked and are left out. Blakely 2012 describes a patient homozygous for MPV17 P98L whose neuropathy came with leukoencephalopathy and liver involvement; the authors likened this to classic Navajo neurohepatopathy. I described this case only for contrast and did not list it as a CMT2EE variant. That paper gives the nucleotide change two different ways (c.2898C>T in the text, c.298C>T in the figure legend), so I did not cite it. No HGNC reference data was supplied, so the intro does not give the gene MIM number or chromosome location.
